releases.title: Alchemy Pay Secures Mississippi Money Transmitter License, Expanding U.S. Regulatory Coverage to 20 States
releases.body:
HONG KONG, Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Alchemy Pay, a world-leading fiat-crypto payment solution provider, has secured a Money Transmitter License (MTL) in Mississippi, granted by the Mississippi Department of Banking and Consumer Finance. With this addition, Alchemy Pay now holds money transmitter licenses in 20 U.S. states, marking another milestone in the company's ongoing efforts to strengthen its regulatory foundation and expand its compliant payment network across the United States.

The Mississippi MTL establishes an additional regulatory authorization for Alchemy Pay's applicable money transmission activities in the state, supporting its efforts to connect traditional financial systems with the digital asset economy. Alchemy Pay continues to pursue additional state licenses, with applications under review in multiple jurisdictions. License information can be verified through NMLS Consumer Access by searching for "Alchemy Pay."

The expanded U.S. regulatory footprint supports Alchemy Pay's broader strategy to facilitate fiat-to-crypto and crypto-to-fiat transactions, expand access to its payment services, and strengthen its presence in key markets. It also pushes forward the company's ongoing development of its stablecoin initiatives and Alchemy Chain, a stablecoin-focused Layer 1 blockchain designed to support global stablecoin payments and financial applications. The network aims to advance a compliant infrastructure for stablecoin-based payments across global markets, while any future stablecoin issuance remains subject to applicable regulatory requirements.

Beyond the United States, Alchemy Pay has continued to advance its regulatory presence across key financial markets. Its milestones include Digital Currency Exchange Provider (DCEP) registration in Australia, Electronic Financial Business registration in South Korea, and admission to Switzerland's VQF as a recognized self-regulatory organization (SRO). In Hong Kong, Alchemy Pay has also advanced its regulatory capabilities through its investment in HTF Securities Limited, an SFC-regulated firm, supporting the development of virtual asset-related services within the applicable licensing framework.

These achievements reflect Alchemy Pay's continued commitment to building a robust compliance framework across jurisdictions. As regulatory clarity develops across the global digital asset industry, the company will continue to strengthen its licensing portfolio and payment infrastructure to support the responsible growth of fiat-crypto services and stablecoin-based financial applications.

About Alchemy Pay

Founded in 2017, Alchemy Pay is a payment gateway that seamlessly connects crypto with traditional fiat currencies for businesses, developers, and end users. With its offerings including On & Off-Ramp, Web3 Digital Bank, NFT Checkout and its newly launched RWA platform, Alchemy Pay supports fiat payments in 173 countries.

The Ramp is a one-stop solution to buy and sell crypto and fiat, easily integrated by platforms and dApps according to requirements. The RWA platform allows global users to invest in tokenized real-world assets using local fiat currencies, lowering entry barriers and democratizing access to traditional financial instruments. Our Web3 Digital Bank supports Web3 enterprises by providing multi-fiat accounts and instant fiat-crypto conversion capabilities. Additionally, the NFT Checkout enables direct purchases of NFTs using fiat payment methods. ACH is the Alchemy Pay network token on the Ethereum blockchain.

releases.title: Barksdale BT1 Temperature Transmitter: Fast-Response, Intrinsically Safe RTD Transmitter with Analog Outputs
releases.body:
Compact stainless-steel temperature transmitter for hydraulic, mobile, oil and gas, and factory automation equipment

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Barksdale Control Products today announced the BT1 Temperature Transmitter, a compact RTD temperature transmitter for fast-response sensing in aggressive media and high-cycle environments. The BT1 comes with analog output options, and intrinsically safe CSA and ATEX for hazardous locations.

Built around a Class B PT100 element in a stainless-steel housing, the BT1 measures process temperatures from -40°C to 200°C (-40°F to 392°F). It is designed for drift-resistant performance and withstands 20 g vibration across three axes and a 1-meter free fall.

KEY FEATURES

  • Fast response: Compact stainless-steel construction for fast-response temperature sensing in aggressive media and high-cycle environments.
  • Flexible outputs: Analog options for modern platforms, including 4–20 mA and voltage outputs.
  • Hazardous-location approvals: Intrinsically safe CSA (C1D1) and ATEX (Ex ia) options.
  • Rugged design: Reverse-polarity and overvoltage protection, with IP65 or IP67 ingress protection depending on the electrical connector.

WHERE THE BT1 FITS

The BT1 is built for hydraulic and pneumatic systems, heavy mobile equipment, OEM factory automation, wellhead tubing, casing and BOP systems, fracking trucks, natural gas compressors and turbines, and mobile hydraulics.

"Hazardous-area approval shouldn't mean overpaying. The BT1 extends our temperature portfolio with a cost-effective option customers can trust," said Frieda Hovsepian, VP Sales and Marketing, Barksdale Control Products.

To review our BT1 Temperature Transmitter Data Sheet, please visit: 

https://www.barksdale.com/products/temperature/bt1-temperature-transmitter?utm_source=prnewsletter&utm_medium=news&utm_campaign=bt1_press_release

ABOUT BARKSDALE CONTROL PRODUCTS

Barksdale Control Products, a subsidiary of Crane Company, is a global leader in precision fluid-control instrumentation. For more than 70 years, Barksdale has designed switches, transducers, regulators and valves for industrial automation, energy and transportation applications.

OTTAWA, ON, Oct. 15, 2026 /CNW/ -- As immigration continues to drive Canadian population growth, understanding how newcomers engage with media and technology is essential for organizations navigating this shifting market.

The MTM Newcomers has released its 2026 data, focusing on the media behaviors, technology adoption, and settlement activities of individuals who have arrived in Canada within the past five years.  Our latest data highlights the evolving landscape of an expanding demographic that currently accounts for nearly one-quarter of the national population.
releases.title: Canadian Newcomers Adopt AI and Short-Form Video at Nearly Double the Rate of Canadian-Born Residents, Finds Latest MTM Report
releases.body:
OTTAWA, ON, Oct. 15, 2026 /CNW/ -- As immigration continues to drive Canadian population growth, understanding how newcomers engage with media and technology is essential for organizations navigating this shifting market.

The MTM Newcomers has released its 2026 data, focusing on the media behaviors, technology adoption, and settlement activities of individuals who have arrived in Canada within the past five years.  Our latest data highlights the evolving landscape of an expanding demographic that currently accounts for nearly one-quarter of the national population.

Highlights from the 2026 MTM Newcomers season include:
  • Widespread Adoption of Short-Form Video: Nine in ten newcomers watch short-form vertical video across platforms like YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, Snapchat Spotlight, and TikTok. Newcomers are nearly 50% more likely to watch short-form video than are Canadian-born respondents, showing double the likelihood to use YouTube Shorts and five times the likelihood to use Snapchat Spotlight.
  • High Engagement with Artificial Intelligence: Four-fifths of newcomers use AI tools, which is nearly double the rate observed among Canadian-born respondents. International students and temporary workers show the highest adoption levels, leveraging a wider variety of AI platforms including Claude, DeepSeek, Perplexity, and Meta AI at more than double the rate of Canadian-born users.
  • Personal Connections Drive Consumer Choices: Newcomers rely heavily on personal recommendations when selecting essential services. They are nearly eight times as likely to choose a grocery store based on word-of-mouth from people they know, twice as likely to choose a cellphone provider based on a recommendation, and four times as likely to pick a provider where an acquaintance works.

releases.title: Open-Source Model Accelerates Global Progress in Medical Video AI
releases.body:
SHANGHAI, Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Through an open-source model, a public dataset and benchmark, and the MedVidU Challenge, a global research competition, researchers worldwide now share a common foundation for advancing medical video AI. The Challenge drew 75 teams from 18 countries and regions across five continents, bringing diverse ideas and approaches into an ecosystem shaped by the wider research community.

Participants represented leading universities, medical institutions, and technology companies, including Harvard Medical School, the University of Oxford, LMU University Hospital, Nanyang Technological University, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, The University of Hong Kong, and NVIDIA.

Supporting this community-driven momentum is a broader effort by United Imaging Intelligence (UII) to create the shared resources and platforms needed for medical video AI research to advance at scale.

Building an Open Foundation for Global Collaboration

Medical video understanding remains one of AI's most demanding frontiers, requiring precise spatial awareness, complex temporal reasoning, and rigorous clinical accuracy. Progress has often been constrained by limited clinical data and the high cost of expert annotation.

UII is addressing these barriers through an open framework designed to make research progress measurable and global collaboration more accessible. In April, following the acceptance of its MedGRPO research at CVPR 2026, UII released uAI NEXUS MedVLM and open-sourced 6,245 MedVidBench test samples. These samples are part of a broader research collection of 531,850 video-instruction pairs that UII annotated using eight existing, publicly available medical video datasets. Access to each component is subject to its release terms and the applicable source-data licenses.

Alongside the model and dataset, UII launched the MedVidBench public leaderboard, which evaluates models across ten metrics, including next-action prediction, skill assessment, and spatiotemporal grounding. Together, these resources gave researchers a common starting point and a consistent way to compare and refine their models.

To turn this shared foundation into collective progress, UII co-launched the MedVidU Challenge with the University of Strasbourg and the Technical University of Munich in summer 2026. UII also released a second MedVidBench batch of 6,270 test samples.

Within approximately three months of its latest release, MedVidBench surpassed 30,000 downloads and received citations from researchers around the world, reflecting growing interest from the global research community.

Uniting Global Expertise to Explore New Frontiers

According to the latest leaderboard, four teams advanced to the final stage of the Challenge. Two teams were invited to present their findings at the ECCV 2026 MedVidU Workshop, held in Malmö, Sweden in September.

The Workshop also featured oral presentations of two accepted papers exploring new ways to expand training resources for surgical AI and advance surgical skill assessment. Broader discussions brought together perspectives from biomedical engineering and robotics, highlighting emerging directions in medical video AI.

Surgical and clinical procedures are routinely recorded, yet much of this video remains underused. Medical video AI could unlock new clinical value, supporting surgical training through structured feedback, assisting with intraoperative safety checks, and streamlining postoperative review and documentation, with potential applications in nursing care and remote mentoring.

UII is building an open ecosystem of shared resources, transparent evaluation, global competition, and research exchange to help translate advances in medical video AI into clinical practice.
